title: People burn free money to punish unfairness
hook: Someone offers you a tiny slice of free money. Refuse, and you both get nothing. Most people refuse.
caption: People burn free money to punish unfairness. In the ultimatum game, offers below about 20% are usually rejected even though rejecting means getting nothing (Camerer 2003).

claims.text: Offers below about 20% are rejected about half the time

scenes.say: Someone offers you a tiny slice of free money. Refuse, and you both get nothing. Most people refuse.
The ultimatum game: one person proposes a split, the other accepts or rejects. Reject, and nobody gets anything.
Economic theory says take anything. It's more than zero.
In reality, offers below about 20% are usually rejected.
scenes.note: Sources: Güth et al. (1982); Camerer (2003), Behavioral Game Theory

scenes.say: Humans don't just maximise money. We'll pay to punish unfairness.
When splitting a deal, don't offer the minimum they'll accept. Offer what they'll call fair.

takeaway: When splitting a deal, don't offer the minimum they'll accept. Offer what they'll call fair.
